title.narrative: Output 6.1. Increased capacity of Member States to promote investments in the care economy and a more balanced sharing of family responsibilities

description.narrative:
Between June and December 2023, the National Confederation of Employers (CNPM) pilot-tested the application of the new regulations on onsite childcare services by supporting the setting up of a childcare facility in two affiliated enterprises. Based on this experience, CNPM drafted a policy document highlighting what did and did not work and making specific recommendations for the amendment of the regulations. On 27 July 2023, CNPM organized a workshop, attended by 100 representatives of enterprises, to inform about the latest legal provisions related to establishing and operating onsite childcare facilities and showcase compelling examples that demonstrate the potential benefits, values and return of investment for companies that choose to implement such childcare services. Between January and April 2023 the ILO conducted a Market System Analysis of the childcare sector in Moldova. On April 2023, a validation workshop bringing together 50 participants was organized. One day was devoted to discussing the implementation of the two modalities of childcare provided by the private sector: home-based nurseries and onsite kindergartens.
On July, 2023 the ILO supported CNPM in the organization of the workshop to inform enterprises about the new regulations and present the international best practices. Likewise, the ILO assisted CNSM in the design of information materials and the elaboration of a guide for enterprises interested in setting up childcare facilities.

Output 6.1. Increased capacity of Member States to promote investments in the care economy and a more balanced sharing of family responsibilities

description.narrative:
On 16, November 2022, Government Decision 785/2022 on the National Employment Program for 2022-2026 and the Action Plan for its implementation was approved. Objective 1 of the NEP aims to increase the activity and employment rates of women with family responsibilities by 3% and 4% respectively by 2026, and one of the indicators is to increase the share of children up to 3 years of age, including refugee children from Ukraine, in care services to 20% by 2026. The National Employment Program is a gender-responsive employment program with economic dimensions which supports the creation of decent employment. In December 2022 the Law 367/2022 on alternative childcare services was endorsed. The Law establishes 3 new modalities of childcare provision: (i) on-site kindergartens supported by the employers; (ii) individual nannies (iii) family-type childcare services. In December 2022, the National Program on childcare services for children up to 3 years of age 2023-2026 was approved. It aims at expanding public creche services, supporting the creation of alternative childcare services and increasing the number of private creches. During 2022, the ILO assisted the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection in mainstreaming gender equality in the employment diagnostic conducted prior to the design of the National Employment Program 2022-2026. Moreover, it provided assistance to the MLSP in defining policy priorities, including Objective 1 on the participation of women in the labor market.
During 2023 the ILO has provided support to the implementation of the National Programme and its Action Plan (AP). The ILO actively participated in the six working groups (legal framework, individual nannies, family-type childcare services, workplace services, communication and e-platform of childcare services) established to ensure effective coordination and monitoring of the AP's implementation.

description.narrative: On 2 August 2023 Government Decision No 572/2023 on the organisation and functioning of alternative childcare services was passed. On December, 2023 a methodological benchmark for training curriculum was accepted by the Ministry of Education and Research. It serves as a guide for the future national providers of qualification programs to develop their own training curriculum for childcare service providers. On 7 December, 2023 Art. 30 (6) of Law 367/2022 was amended to extend the possibility for the nanny to operate based on the entrepreneur patent. This modification will create job opportunities for individual nannies. On 26 December 2023 a policy paper stating normative proposals to improve the social protection of individual nannies was discussed in the Parliamentary Commission on Social Protection. The paper contains recommendations to improve social protection of nannies. Between January and July 2023, the ILO provided technical assistance to the working group commissioned to draft the regulations on the organisation of alternative childcare services. In June 2023 the ILO produced a matrix collecting experiences and good practices from EU countries on the training of individual nannies. This analysis of international experiences served as the basis for the revision of the existing curriculum and qualification standard. In September 2023, the ILO elaborated a formalisation guide detailing the process for the registration of individual childcare providers. This guide was validated through a training of nannies organized in 16 and 17 October and 8 November The ILO provided technical assistance for the drafting of the changes to Law 367/2022. Between June and September 2023, the ILO collected international good practices on social protection for domestic workers and nannies, including an analysis of the EU legislation and social protection schemes. The ILO supported the drafting of the policy paper with normative proposals to improve the social protection of individual carers.

description.narrative: On 28 January 2022 the National Confederation of Trade Unions (CNSM) proposed the initiation of the ratification procedure to the National Commission for Consultation and Collective Bargaining. In December 2022, the National Commission for Consultation and Collective Bargaining confirmed the tripartite commitment to ratification and requested the government to initiate the ratification process. On 31 May 2023, under the auspices of the MLSP, the Parliament of Moldova established a working group bringing together members of parliament, public institutions, employers and workers organizations to discuss amendments to the national legislation to comply with the provisions of Convention num. 190 and lead the implementation of initiatives to promote the ratification of C. 190. The working group has finalised a text which includes several draft amendments to legislation to be submitted to the Parliament along with the draft ratification law, as per the official procedure, by the end of the year. In November 2022 CNSM launched a campaign to promote the ratification of C 190 on the Elimination of violence and harassment at work. On December 28th, 2023 the Moldovan Parliament passed the ratfication law of the ILO Violence and Harassment Convention, 2019 (No.190). During 2023, the Trade Union (CNSM), Employers organization (CNPM), the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, and the Parliament collaborated to enhance awareness and sensitization regarding Convention No. 190. As part of this effort, they actively participated in the ILO global campaign advocating for workplaces free of violence and harassment, with the ultimate goal of ratifying Convention No. 190. In response to the request of the Ministry of Labour and Social Polidy for technical assistance, the ILO updated the 2021 Gap analysis of the legal framework with regards to C.190 and drafted a briefing note containing recommendations for legal changes and a road map for a phased implementation of the Convention. This briefing served as input for the discussions of the working group set up by the Parliament. Moreover, the ILO facilitated the discussions of the working group and assisted in drafting the legal changes to be made to the national legislation. Further, ILO provided support to National Confederation of Trade Unions (CNSM) on the design and implementation of the campaign to promote the ratification of C190. ILO provided techincal support to the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection throughout the ratification process. This support encompassed active participation in working groups and engaging in discussions with relevant authorities. ILO translated and adjusted in Romanian the social media package to advocate for the importance of ratifying ILO; ILO translated and adjusted informational materials regarding the 16 Days Campaign to advocate ratification.
